project.title: Car rental management
project.alt: Actual Fleetdesk dashboard with eight synthetic vehicles, six fictional customers and calculated example rates
project.desc: A polished workspace for vehicle inventory and customer records, with a tested Flask API and an explicitly static public demonstration.
project.built: Developed the original Flask/MySQL coursework into a practical record-management dashboard with a shared browser demonstration.
project.why: Everyday record management depends on clear workflows and consistent data. This prototype brings the interface, API and storage responsibilities together.
how: Browse synthetic vehicles and customers, with summaries calculated from current records.
Create, search, edit and delete records with clear validation, cancellation and confirmation.
Reset the sample workspace, or run the same frontend against the local Flask API and optional MySQL store.
project.demonstrates: Full-stack development, REST endpoints, relational data access and translating a record-management requirement into a usable interface.
project.caption: The verified Fleetdesk dashboard: eight synthetic vehicles, six fictional customers and a calculated €59 mean daily rate. This image is captured from the source revision shown below.
project.result: 13 API/authentication regression tests, an isolated MySQL 8.4 CRUD/authentication integration test, two frontend-rule tests and three browser workflow tests passed before this release. Browser checks cover both Flask and static modes, persistence, duplicates, cancellation, reset, simulated failure recovery and mobile layout. The linked run records the exact revision.
project.limits: All public records are synthetic and stored in the browser. The demo does not run Flask/MySQL, create real rentals, process payments or model fleet availability. Customer vehicle references are descriptive records rather than enforced reservations. Multi-user concurrency and production access controls are outside this educational prototype.
project.technical: One frontend uses a Flask REST adapter or a browser-storage adapter. Existing /cars and /customer routes and integer Price fields are preserved; Price is presented as a whole-euro example daily rate. The MySQL adapter uses bounded pooled connections, parameterized queries, rollback and cleanup. Writes reject duplicate references/pairs and cross-origin requests. Tests cover both adapters, reset, failures and mobile layout.
project.run: Install requirements.txt, set DEMO_MODE=1 and run python CarServer.py. Open http://127.0.0.1:5000. See the README for MySQL configuration and opt-in disposable integration tests.
gallery: Vehicle inventory, search and record actions.

project.demo_disclosure: Public demo: browser-managed synthetic data. The Flask/MySQL implementation is available separately in the source.
